guardrails: none: no citation gate, no critic, fix not forced to need approval
rationale: emailservice latency-90 rose from 0.0046 to 0.2125 (z=+899) and latency-50 rose +1334%, the largest deviations of any series. checkoutservice, which calls emailservice, shows a smaller latency increase (+106%), consistent with propagation, while emailservice cpu is flat (+3.9%) and there are no error or warning logs, so cpu, mem and loss are not supported and delay is the best fit.

proposed_fix.description: Inspect emailservice and its network path for added latency (e.g. network delay injection, a slow downstream dependency, or throttling), and remove the source of the delay. If it is an injected network fault, clear it. Verify by watching emailservice latency-90 return to baseline of about 5 ms. No restart or data deletion is needed.
